The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) members in Ebonyi State have condemned political thuggery and violence and called for issue-based political engagement, peaceful coexistence, and good governance ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The party members made the call during a peaceful road walk organised by Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy in Abakaliki on Friday.
The participants, mainly PDP supporters, walked from the popular Nkaliki area through the Spera-in-doe axis and the Enugu-Abakaliki Expressway in the state capital.
They said the road walk aimed to promote political tolerance, responsible leadership and democratic values in Ebonyi and Nigeria at large.
The participants, who displayed placards bearing various inscriptions, called for support for a sustainable democratic system and good governance.
Some of the inscriptions read: “Say no to thuggery”, “Ebonyi youths stand for peace, not violence” and “We seek a society where citizens can speak, assemble and live without fear”.
Others read: “Our people must speak without fear”, “The people’s rights must be protected” and “The Constitution of Nigeria must not be trampled. Democracy must protect even those who disagree”.

They used the exercise to highlight the need for a peaceful political atmosphere where citizens can freely express their opinions and participate in democratic processes without intimidation or violence.
Mark Onu, national president of Odozi-Obodo Youth Movement, said political activities should be driven by constructive engagement, mutual respect and the collective interest of the people.
He urged political actors to respect opposing views and shun hostility, intimidation and personal attacks.
Nnanna Nwangene, a youth leader, said violence has no place in a democratic society, urging political leaders, supporters and other stakeholders to embrace peaceful conduct before, during and after the 2027 general elections.
Mr Nwangene emphasised the importance of good governance, accountability, transparency and people-oriented policies as essential ingredients for sustainable development.
According to him, elected public office holders must remain accountable to the electorate and ensure that democratic dividends translate into improved living conditions for the people.
Rostick Eze, another leader, said the initiative was designed to encourage young people to take an active interest in governance and demand responsible leadership through peaceful and lawful means.
Mr Eze urged youths in the state to shun political thuggery, hate speech, and other activities that threaten the peace and stability of Ebonyi.
Also speaking at the event, a resident of Ebonyi, Jerry Uhuo, called on political parties and their supporters to prioritise the welfare of citizens and promote an atmosphere conducive to credible elections.
Mr Uhuo further appealed to residents to support initiatives that advance peace, democratic participation and sustainable development.
